title: Self-Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Networks using a Soft Attention Mechanism
affiliations: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA (both authors)
identifier: DOI:10.1016/j.jcp.2022.111722 (analyzed PDF is the arXiv preprint arXiv:2009.04544v5)
subdomain: Self-adaptive (per-training-point) loss weighting via trainable soft attention masks for stiff PDEs; minimax (descent/ascent) training; NTK-based weight analysis; GP-interpolated weights enabling small-batch SGD
industry_context: No industry or company named; academic methods paper (Texas A&M University). Support: D3EM program funded through NSF Award DGE-1545403 and the US Army CCDC Army Research Lab (Acknowledgments, p. 22).
problem_class: forward (all six experiments are forward PDE solves; conclusion motivates extension to forward and inverse modeling)
physics_enforced_exact: General initial-boundary value problem N_{x,t}[u(x,t)] = f(x,t) for x in Omega, t in (0,T]; B_{x,t}[u(x,t)] = g(x,t) on dOmega; u(x,0) = h(x) (eqs. 1-3). Concrete cases: viscous Burgers u_t + u*u_x - (0.01/pi)*u_xx = 0, x in [-1,1], t in [0,1], u(0,x) = -sin(pi*x), u(t,-1) = u(t,1) = 0 (eqs. 22-24); Helmholtz u_xx + u_yy + k^2*u - q(x,y) = 0 on [-1,1]^2 with u = 0 on all boundaries and forcing q(x,y) giving exact solution u = sin(a1*x)*sin(a2*y), a1 = a2 = 4 (eqs. 25-28); Allen-Cahn reaction-diffusion u_t - 0.0001*u_xx + 5u^3 - 5u = 0, x in [-1,1], t in [0,1], u(0,x) = x^2*cos(pi*x), periodic BCs u(t,-1) = u(t,1), u_x(t,-1) = u_x(t,1) (eqs. 29-32); 2D viscous Burgers system u_t + u*u_x + v*u_y = nu*(u_xx + u_yy), v_t + v*u_x + v*u_y = nu*(v_xx + v_yy) (as printed), nu = 0.002, with manufactured solutions u = 3/4 - 1/4*[1+exp((-4x+4y-t)/(32*nu))]^-1 and v = 3/4 + 1/4*[1+exp((-4x+4y-t)/(32*nu))]^-1 following [30] (eqs. 34-37), only initial conditions enforced; 1D wave u_tt - 4*u_xx = 0 on (0,1)^2, u(0,t) = u(1,t) = 0, u_t(x,0) = 0, u(x,0) = sin(pi*x) + 1/2*sin(4*pi*x), exact solution u = sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*t) + 1/2*sin(4*pi*x)*cos(8*pi*t) (eqs. 38-42, benchmark of [5]); linear advection q_t + ubar*q_x = 0 on (0,L]x(0,T] with Dirichlet BCs and discontinuous initial condition g(x), solution q(x,t) = g(x - ubar*t) (eqs. 66-69).
pde_type: multiple (parabolic: viscous Burgers, Allen-Cahn reaction-diffusion; elliptic: Helmholtz; hyperbolic: 1D wave, linear advection, 2D Burgers system)
dimensionality: 1D+time (Burgers, Allen-Cahn, wave, advection); 2D steady (Helmholtz); 2D+time (2D Burgers system with two velocity-field outputs)
nonlinearity: mixed: strongly nonlinear in Allen-Cahn (cubic reaction term 5u^3 - 5u producing sharp phase transitions) and Burgers (nonlinear advection u*u_x, attenuated shock); linear in Helmholtz, wave, and advection cases
bcs_ic_handled: All IC/BC terms enter as soft least-squares penalties each multiplied by a trainable self-adaptive weight: L_0 on u(x_i^0,0) vs h, L_b on B_{x,t}[u] vs g, plus the residual term L_r. Allen-Cahn: periodic BCs enforced through the combined penalty (1/N_b) sum g(lambda_b^i)*(|u(1,t_i^b) - u(-1,t_i^b)|^2 + |u_x(1,t_i^b) - u_x(-1,t_i^b)|^2) (eq. 33), with boundary weights held fixed at 1 and only initial and residual weights trained (periodicity makes N_b = 200 boundary points). 2D Burgers: only initial conditions enforced, BCs deliberately not enforced (manufactured solution on the whole domain). Sensor-data term L_s is never masked ('since these data consist of noisy observations, weighting them requires extra care to avoid overfitting', p. 5). Prior knowledge injected via weight initialization, e.g. Allen-Cahn IC weights drawn from U(0,100) because the IC is hard to fit (p. 5, p. 10).
enforcement_mechanism: soft-penalty, but with a fundamentally new weighting scheme: fully-trainable per-training-point weights producing a multiplicative soft attention mask; the loss is minimized w.r.t. network weights w and simultaneously maximized w.r.t. the self-adaptive weights lambda (saddle-point/minimax training, eqs. 14-17); conclusion shows this is formally equivalent to a penalty (boundary) method for PDE-constrained optimization with monotonically-nondecreasing trainable penalty coefficients
enforcement_details: Residuals formed by reverse-mode automatic differentiation of the network output (Sec. 2.1). Loss (eqs. 10-13): L(w,lambda_r,lambda_b,lambda_0) = L_s(w) + L_r(w,lambda_r) + L_b(w,lambda_b) + L_0(w,lambda_0), with each masked term (1/2N_p) sum m(lambda_p^i)*|unmasked squared term|^2, where m on (0,infinity) is a nonnegative, differentiable, strictly increasing mask function (e.g. polynomial m(lambda) = c*lambda^q with q = 2 or 4, or smooth/sharp sigmoidal masks; Fig. 1; denoted g(lambda) in eq. 33). Gradient descent on w (learning rate eta^k) is alternated with gradient ascent on lambda_r, lambda_b, lambda_0 (separate learning rates beta_p^k); since grad_lambda L = (1/2)*m'(lambda)*|unmasked loss|^2 (eqs. 18-20), each weight grows in proportion to its squared unmasked loss, so difficult regions of the solution are automatically weighted more. Any term's weights can be fixed at 1 (boundary weights in Allen-Cahn). SGD extension (Sec. 5): because weights are attached to specific points, small-batch SGD is enabled by predicting self-adaptive weights of newly sampled points with Gaussian-process regression over the space-time domain, producing a continuous self-adaptive weight map; GP fitted with fixed hyperparameters (no automatic tuning), all training points resampled every 100 iterations.
network_architecture: Fully-connected MLPs throughout (no architectural modification; contribution is in the loss/optimization): Burgers [2, 8 hidden layers x 20 neurons, 1] matching [2]; Helmholtz [2,50,50,50,50,1] matching [12]; Allen-Cahn [2,128,128,128,1] matching [4]; wave equation 5 layers x 500 neurons matching [5]; linear advection [2,400,400,400,400,1]; 2D Burgers architecture not specified.
activation_function: tanh (stated explicitly for the wave-equation network; not stated for the other cases)
input_representation: spatio-temporal coordinates (x,t), or (x,y)/(x,y,t) for the 2D cases; no extra features
output_representation: the solution field u directly (two outputs u, v for the 2D Burgers system); no output transforms
loss_terms: L(w,lambda_r,lambda_b,lambda_0) = L_s(w) + L_r(w,lambda_r) + L_b(w,lambda_b) + L_0(w,lambda_0) (eq. 10); L_s = (1/2N_s) sum |u(x_i^s,t_i^s;w) - y_i^s|^2 (unmasked sensor data, eq. 5); L_r = (1/2N_r) sum m(lambda_r^i)*|N_{x,t}[u(x_r^i,t_r^i;w)] - f(x_r^i,t_r^i)|^2 (eq. 11); L_b = (1/2N_b) sum m(lambda_b^i)*|B_{x,t}[u] - g|^2 (eq. 12; replaced by eq. 33 for periodic BCs); L_0 = (1/2N_0) sum m(lambda_0^i)*|u(x_i^0,0) - h(x_i^0)|^2 (eq. 13). Standard weighted loss L = lambda_s*L_s + lambda_r*L_r + lambda_b*L_b + lambda_0*L_0 (eq. 9) recovered as the special case when all per-point weights of a component are equal (p. 19).
loss_weighting: self-adaptive attention (the paper's proposal): per-point trainable weights updated by gradient ascent with constant separate learning rates beta (5e-3 in Burgers/Helmholtz/Allen-Cahn; wave: 0.01 residual, 0.05 IC on u_t, 0.25 other IC/BC points on u; advection: 0.1), side-by-side with network-weight descent; initialization encodes priors (Allen-Cahn IC weights U(0,100), residual U(0,1); Burgers/Helmholtz weights U(0,1)); weights held constant during L-BFGS; sensor-data term unmasked. NTK analysis (Sec. 6): eigenvalues of K_pp*Gamma_p are bounded between m(lambda_min)*gamma_p and m(lambda_max)*gamma_p (eqs. 61-62), so SA weights equalize eigenvalue magnitudes across loss terms and also smooth the shape of the eigenvalue distribution (unlike traditional whole-component scaling). Practical recipe (Sec. 4.5): small network learning rates (~1e-5) and larger self-adaptive learning rates (1e-3 to 1e-1).
sampling_strategy: Uniform random collocation points with fixed counts: Burgers N_0 = 100, N_b = 200, N_r = 10,000; Helmholtz N_b = 400 (100 per boundary edge), N_r = 100,000 sampled from a 1001x1001 mesh (1,002,001 total points), no IC; Allen-Cahn N_0 = 100, N_b = 100 (200 periodic boundary points), N_r = 20,000; wave N_0 = 100, N_b = 100, N_r = 300 (same hyperparameters as [5]). SGD variant (Sec. 5): all training points resampled every 100 iterations with GP-interpolated self-adaptive weights.
optimizer_schedule: Adam (TensorFlow 2.3) followed by L-BFGS quasi-Newton (Liu & Nocedal [24]), consistent with baseline PINN practice; self-adaptive weights updated only during Adam steps and held constant during L-BFGS. Burgers: 10k Adam + 10k L-BFGS; Helmholtz: 10k Adam + 10k L-BFGS (vs 40k Adam in [12]); Allen-Cahn: Adam, 10k training iterations shown in Fig. 12; 2D Burgers: 35k Adam at lr 1e-5 + 20k L-BFGS; wave (SGD variant): Adam at lr 1e-5 for 80,000 iterations; advection: 10k Adam at network lr 0.001.
training_compute: Single Nvidia V100 GPU, TensorFlow 2.3: Burgers 90 ms/iteration; Allen-Cahn 65 ms/iteration; advection average 7 s per 1000 iterations; wave Table 1 average wall-clock over 10 runs: 850.75 s (fixed weights, no SGD) to 1207.85 s (self-adaptive + SGD).
data_regime: physics-only (no solution data in any experiment; the sensor-data term L_s exists in the formulation but all cases use only PDE residual + IC/BC points generated from manufactured exact solutions)
datasets_used: Analytic benchmark PDEs: 1D viscous Burgers; 2D Helmholtz (a1 = a2 = 4, benchmark of [12]); Allen-Cahn reaction-diffusion (benchmark of [4]); 2D viscous Burgers system (manufactured solution following DeepXDE [30]); 1D wave equation (benchmark of [5]); linear advection with several discontinuities in the initial condition (numerical example of [5])
baselines_compared: Baseline PINN (Raissi et al. [2]); nonadaptive weighting (C >> 1 on IC) and time-adaptive scheme of Wight & Zhao [4]; learning-rate-annealing weighting of Wang, Teng & Perdikaris [12]; NTK weighting of Wang, Yu & Perdikaris [5] (result quoted, not rerun); fixed-weight PINN and baseline PINN each with and without SGD (wave Table 1); classical solvers not compared.
evaluation_metrics: Relative L2 error (eq. 21: sqrt(sum|u-U|^2)/sqrt(sum|U|^2)) against the high-fidelity solution on a fine mesh of N_v points, averaged over 10 random restarts with standard deviation; average training time in seconds; NTK eigenvalue spectra of K_uu, K_utt and their masked versions Gamma_r*K_uu, Gamma_r*K_utt at training times tau = 1000, 5000, 10000 (Fig. 17).
key_quantitative_results: - 1D viscous Burgers (8x20 MLP, 10k Adam + 10k L-BFGS, 10 restarts): L2 = 4.80e-4 +- 1.01e-4 vs 6.7e-4 reported for the baseline PINN of [2], using only 20% as many training iterations with an identical architecture; learned weights concentrate at the sharp discontinuity x = 0 (Fig. 4). - 2D Helmholtz ([2,50,50,50,50,1], 10k Adam + 10k L-BFGS, N_r = 100k): L2 = 3.2e-3 +- 2.2e-4 vs 1.4e-1 for the baseline PINN and 2.54e-3 to 2.7e-2 for learning-rate-annealing schemes in [12], with 10k+10k iterations vs 40k Adam in [12]. - Allen-Cahn ([2,128,128,128,1], 10 restarts): L2 = 2.1e-2 +- 1.2e-2 vs 8.0e-2 +- 0.56e-2 (time-adaptive scheme of [4]), 96.15e-2 +- 2.50e-2 (baseline PINN) and 49.61e-2 +- 2.50e-2 (nonadaptive weighting C = 100); SA-PINN reaches an IC loss two orders of magnitude smaller than the baseline (Fig. 12) and its learned weights show more attention early in time, 'discovering' the time-irreversibility of the PDE (Figs. 9-10). - 1D wave with SGD + GP-interpolated weights (5x500 tanh MLP, network lr 1e-5, 80k iterations, 10 restarts, Table 1): L2 = 0.0295 +- 0.0070 (self-adaptive + SGD) vs 0.2079 +- 0.0624 (fixed weights + SGD) and 0.4513 +- 0.0255 (baseline + SGD); without SGD all variants fail (0.3792-0.8105). The SA + SGD result is an order of magnitude better than fixed-weight + SGD but larger than the 0.01 reported in [5]. - Linear advection with discontinuous IC ([2,400,400,400,400,1], 10k Adam): SA-PINN approximates the solution within 5% L2 error while the baseline PINN 'failed to grasp even the rough structure of the solution'; masked NTK eigenvalues of K_uu and K_utt become closely matched in scale (Fig. 17). - 2D viscous Burgers (2D+time): L2 ~ 3e-3 for both u and v at t = 1/3 and t = 2/3, capturing the attenuated shock; the baseline PINN's L-BFGS failed to converge for the same iteration budget.
errors_reported: Burgers rel. L2 = 4.80e-4 +- 1.01e-4 (SA-PINN) vs 6.7e-4 (baseline [2]); Helmholtz rel. L2 = 3.2e-3 +- 2.2e-4 (SA-PINN) vs 1.4e-1 (baseline PINN) and 2.54e-3 to 2.7e-2 (LRA variants, both from [12]); Allen-Cahn rel. L2 = 2.1e-2 +- 1.2e-2 (SA-PINN) vs 8.0e-2 +- 0.56e-2 (time-adaptive [4]), 96.15e-2 +- 2.50e-2 (baseline PINN) and 49.61e-2 +- 2.50e-2 (nonadaptive C = 100); wave L2 = 0.0295 +- 0.0070 (self-adaptive + SGD), 0.2079 +- 0.0624 (fixed + SGD), 0.8105 +- 0.1591 (self-adaptive, no SGD), 0.7296 +- 0.1421 (fixed, no SGD), 0.3792 +- 0.0162 (baseline, no SGD), 0.4513 +- 0.0255 (baseline + SGD); 2D Burgers L2 ~ 3e-3 (u and v at t = 1/3 and 2/3); advection within 5% L2 after 10k Adam iterations.
speedup_claims: Accuracy-per-epoch claims, not wall-clock speedups: 'the SA-PINN outperformed other state-of-the-art PINN algorithm in L2 error, while using a smaller number of training epochs' (abstract); Burgers solved with 'only 20% as many training iterations' as the baseline at lower error; Helmholtz with 10k Adam + 10k L-BFGS vs 40k Adam in [12]. Wall-clock trade-off on the wave problem: self-adaptive + SGD averages 1207.85 s vs 1057.04 s for baseline + SGD (Table 1) - more time per run, far lower error.
ablations: (i) Mask-function shape study (Fig. 1, Sec. 3): polynomial masks (q = 2, 4) must be kept below suitable values to avoid numerical overflow; sigmoidal masks avoid overflow and can be sharp, but excessively sharp ones suffer vanishing gradients, so they should be avoided. (ii) Fixed-weight control on the wave PDE (Sec. 5): constants matching the final average self-adaptive values (1.0 residual, 5.0 IC on u_t, 50.0 other IC/BC) give L2 = 0.2079 +- 0.0624 with SGD vs 0.0295 +- 0.0070 for trainable weights - the gain comes from adaptivity, not just weight magnitude. (iii) SGD vs no-SGD on wave: without SGD the SA-PINN fails (0.8105), motivating the GP weight-map extension. (iv) Weight-initialization study on Allen-Cahn (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 10): with all weights initialized U(0,1), IC weights still grow faster than residual weights on their own, matching the time-irreversibility prior; U(0,100) IC initialization (Fig. 8) encodes that prior explicitly. (v) NTK eigenvalue tracking (Fig. 17, tau = 1000/5000/10000): masked eigenvalues of K_uu and K_utt become closely matched in scale under SA-PINN, and the eigenvalue-distribution shape is equalized, not merely scaled as with whole-component weighting.
stated_limitations: Sec. 7 (p. 20-21): 'there is much that is not known yet about this class of algorithms. While the empirical results observed here show significant promise, and despite the fact that an initial analysis based on the NTK is provided, more theoretical justification is desirable, which will be part of future work. In addition, the use of standard off-the-shelf optimization algorithms for training deep neural networks, such as Adam, may not be appropriate, since those algorithms were mostly developed for traditional deep learning applications; obtaining optimization algorithms specifically tailored to Self-Adaptive PINNs, and indeed PINNs in general, in an open problem. Finally, the relationship between Self-Adaptive PINNs and constrained-optimization problems is likely a fruitful topic of future study.' Sec. 5: the SA + SGD wave L2 of 2.95% 'is however larger than the one reported in [5]' (0.01); adaptive tuning of the GP hyperparameters is left as future work. Sec. 4.5: better results 'could potentially be obtained by using learning rate scheduling'; effective training requires small network learning rates (1e-5) and larger self-adaptive learning rates (1e-3 to 1e-1) - empirical guidance rather than a principled rule.
failure_modes: (1) Baseline PINN failure on 'stiff' PDEs with sharp space transitions or fast time evolution (Allen-Cahn, wave, advection): gradient descent on the linearly-scalarized multi-part loss is 'a greedy procedure that may latch onto some of the components at the expense of others, which creates an imbalance in the rate of descent' (Sec. 2.2). (2) The full-batch SA-PINN itself fails on the 1D wave equation (L2 = 0.8105) because weights are attached to specific training points; small-batch SGD requires the GP weight-map extension (Sec. 5). (3) Baseline PINN L-BFGS fails to converge on the 2D Burgers system, while the SA-PINN 'appears to stabilize the training process, allowing the L-BFGS optimizer to converge' (Sec. 4.4). (4) Polynomial mask functions risk numerical overflow at large lambda; overly sharp sigmoidal masks cause vanishing gradients during training, particularly at lower starting weight values (Sec. 3). (5) Oscillatory residue loss during SA-PINN training reflects competing dynamics between the self-adaptive IC and residual terms (Fig. 12).
reproducibility: Full implementation publicly available at https://github.com/levimcclenny/SA-PINNs (footnote, p. 6), implemented in TensorFlow 2.3 and included in the open-source TensorDiffEq library (McClenny, Haile, Braga-Neto, arXiv:2103.16034, cited [25]); architecture, point counts, learning rates, and weight initializations are given per experiment; all L2 results averaged over 10 random restarts with standard deviations. No random seeds stated. Hardware: Nvidia V100.
quotable_finding: the SA-PINN outperformed other state-of-the-art PINN algorithm in L2 error, while using a smaller number of training epochs. (p. 1)
relevance_rqs: RQ2 (components): canonical loss-weighting/self-adaptive-attention component - per-point trainable weights with descent/ascent (minimax) training, mask-function design, and GP weight maps enabling SGD; RQ3 (physics+mechanism): physics remains a soft-penalty autodiff residual, but the paper explains and fixes why soft-penalty multi-term losses train unevenly (trainable penalty coefficients = penalty/boundary method; NTK analysis showing eigenvalue equalization across K_uu and K_utt); RQ4 (reviews+reliability): key reference on PINN training reliability for stiff PDEs, with baseline and weighting-variant failures documented side-by-side over 10 restarts; RQ1 (problem classes/industries): only forward math benchmarks - no industrial application.
manuscript_section: S4 methods (adaptive loss-weighting strategies, training dynamics/optimizers, NTK analysis); T1 component taxonomy (loss-weighting column) and T2 training-methods table; F2/F4-type figures on failure modes and weighting mechanisms; reliability discussion (RQ4).
cross_paper_links: builds-on PINN-A01 (Raissi, Perdikaris, Karniadakis 2019, cited [2]: baseline PINN whose Burgers benchmark, architecture, and 6.7e-4 error are directly reused); directly compares-to and extends PINN-A06 (Wang, Yu, Perdikaris, 'When and why PINNs fail to train: A NTK perspective', cited [5]): reuses its wave and advection benchmarks and hyperparameters, generalizes its NTK expression (Lemma 3.1) to SA-PINNs via eq. 58, and reports its SA + SGD wave error 0.0295 as larger than PINN-A06's 0.01; compares-to Wight & Zhao adaptive-time-weighting Allen-Cahn PINN (cited [4], approach used verbatim for comparison) and Wang, Teng, Perdikaris learning-rate annealing (cited [12]) and Liu & Wang minimax weighting (cited [18]) as closest prior weighting schemes - SA-PINN differs by weighting individual points rather than whole loss components; builds on Jacot et al. NTK (cited [35]); implemented in TensorDiffEq (cited [25]); 2D Burgers example taken from DeepXDE (Lu et al., cited [30]).
notes_caveats: Analyzed PDF is arXiv:2009.04544v5 (18 Jun 2024) of the JCP article ('Published in Journal of Computational Physics, Vol. 474, 111722' printed on p. 1); page numbers refer to the preprint pagination. Same paper as slice-B record B05 (this row covers both slices A+B). All experiments are analytic math benchmarks at most 2D+time: no experimental data, no comparison to classical numerical solvers (FEM/FVM), no inverse problems despite the concluding motivation. The headline full-batch SA-PINN (Adam + L-BFGS) actually FAILS on the wave equation (L2 0.8105); the strong wave result requires the separate SGD + GP variant, which is also the only case with a wall-clock disadvantage and still does not beat the NTK weighting of PINN-A06 (0.01). Per-point weights add N_r + N_b + N_0 extra trainable parameters and the paper gives no memory/overhead accounting; hyperparameter sensitivity is acknowledged (Sec. 4.5). Mask-function notation is inconsistent in the preprint (m(lambda) in eqs. 11-13 vs g(lambda) in eq. 33). Eq. (35) for the 2D Burgers v-momentum is printed as 'v_t + v*u_x + v*u_y' (the standard form would be u*v_x + v*v_y); transcribed as printed. Strengths: results averaged over 10 restarts with std, identical architectures/point counts to the baselines it beats, and both empirical and NTK-theoretical support - the definitive reference for per-point adaptive loss weighting (~1300 citations).
